title: Can you look like Zodd from Berserk in real life? (ANIME WORKOUTS)
summary: NH presents a 5-day upper/lower/arm program to build a physique modelled on Zodd from Berserk, prioritising biceps, triceps, shoulders, traps/yoke and neck, with chest and posterior chain de-prioritised but not ignored. Compared with his Guts program it adds a second lower day plus extra arm and yoke work, and is heavily autoregulated with exercise options and two weekly templates.
claims: Bodybuilding is a game of illusion: you can approximate an anime physique like Zodd's by matching its muscular distribution, minus the inhuman proportions
Zodd program prioritises biceps, triceps, shoulders and upper back/yoke; abs, forearms, quads, erectors and calves get decent work; chest and posterior chain are de-prioritised but never ignored
Compared with the Guts program, the Zodd program trains legs twice a week and adds extra arm and yoke work, going from 4 to 5 training days
Going from 4 to 5 days raises both volume and frequency, making fatigue harder to manage; watch your recovery

Beginners or those who never ran his programs should start with his novice, Baki or Tokita Ohma programs; his methods are hard on people with low work capacity and this one requires on-the-fly autoregulation
Split: Upper 1, Lower 1, rest, Upper 2, Lower 2, Arm day (Mon/Tue/Thu/Fri/Sat); a second template reorders the same days starting with lower
Neck: 100-180 reps of neck curls per week across 10-12 sets, never below 10 or above 20 reps per set, max 4 sets per day, superset with other lifts
Capping neck sets per day prevents doing all reps in one day, which would just be junk volume, and maximises recovery
Rack/block pulls are done for 12-15 reps from below the knee to stretch the upper back and grow traps while limiting posterior chain work
The single vertical press gets 3-5 sets of 6-12, almost double the volume of 3 sets, to let you add shoulder volume if desired
Overhead triceps extensions should be done behind the head to target the long head
Do not skip calf raises; if you want big calves you have to train them
Lat pulldowns in this program use pronated or neutral grip, not supinated
Extra quad work should come from movements that deload the lower back and stretch the quads, like single-leg press or split squats
No straight horizontal press on upper 2 because Zodd's shoulders dwarf his chest; use incline or Viking press (Viking press only if you need no chest work)
Heavy pressing programs need direct external rotation work like face pulls to keep shoulders balanced and healthy
Skull crushers/French press are needed because presses do not fully cover the triceps
Chest flies and preacher curls get a wide 8-20 rep range because they are risky with heavy weight and you arrive pre-fatigued, so strength drops fast
Deadlifts only need 3x5 to be effective; RDL alternative is 4x8-12
Hang or power cleans are not that hard to learn; pick the one you enjoy most
Towel grip hold: loop a towel through a plate, stand and hold 15-30 seconds
Training the upper back almost daily is hard but the area can take it once habituated; to grow a huge upper back you must raise frequency, rotating which areas get hit and managing lower back fatigue
A good arm day for advanced lifters includes compound movements (close-grip bench, dips, rows) for more upper body volume
Forearms should be trained in static/hold, crush grip and elbow/wrist flexion positions for complete development
High frequency for biceps, triceps, shoulders, traps and neck is recoverable because daily volume per area stays moderate
Do not ignore weaker areas like chest, glutes and hamstrings or the physique will look weird
Getting close to Zodd's physique takes years of struggle; whether you believe it is possible or not, you are right
